fish.description: An aggressive predator and one of the most sought sport fish.
fish.fun_fact: Can see colour and uses it to identify and target specific prey.
fish.name: Largemouth Bass

fish.fun_fact: Electric Eels generate shocks of up to 860 volts, enough to stun a horse, and use weaker pulses to navigate and locate prey in complete darkness.
fish.name: Electric Eel

fish.description: One of the most aggressive sharks, equally comfortable in salt and freshwater.
fish.fun_fact: Bull sharks have been found over 4,000 km up the Amazon River, far from the open ocean.
fish.name: Bull Shark

fish.description: A blind hydrothermal-vent crab with hair-covered claws.
fish.fun_fact: Found only at hydrothermal vents. The hairy claws farm bacteria they eat.
fish.name: Yeti Crab

fish.description: A long, predatory deep-sea fish with light-producing barbels.
fish.fun_fact: Lures prey with a glowing barbel. Its teeth are transparent so the lure isn't blocked.
fish.name: Black Dragonfish

fish.description: A small, colorful sunfish common in lakes and ponds.
fish.fun_fact: Can make grunting sounds by grinding their teeth together.
fish.name: Bluegill

fish.fun_fact: Needlefish can leap from water at speeds up to 37 mph and have accidentally impaled fishermen with their needle-like beaks, making them unexpectedly dangerous for such a small fish.
fish.name: Needlefish

fish.description: A ferocious pack hunter known for its slashing, violent strikes.
fish.fun_fact: Will enter a feeding frenzy and continue attacking fish even when completely full, leaving trails of destruction.
fish.name: Bluefish

fish.description: A fast, schooling fish with striking iridescent markings.
fish.fun_fact: Cannot stop swimming or they will suffocate, since they breathe only by moving forward through the water.
fish.name: Atlantic Mackerel

fish.description: A tiny, nearly transparent fish found in staggering numbers throughout the deep ocean.
fish.fun_fact: Bristlemouths may be the most abundant vertebrate on the entire planet, with billions inhabiting the world's deep waters.
fish.name: Bristlemouth

fish.description: A small squid blanketed in photophores that pulse with vivid blue bioluminescent light.
fish.fun_fact: Firefly squid have three types of photoreceptors, one of which may let them perceive colour, a rare ability among cephalopods.
fish.name: Firefly Squid
